parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of gender identity or expression; same-sex conduct decriminalised by 2007 Supreme Court ruling; third-gender self-declaration markers exist; courts have ruled for trans recognition without medical verification; pride events, curriculum inclusion and functioning LGBT organisations show a partly accepting institutional culture. Traveler-facing negatives are indirect: no documented border/document friction against visitors, no facility ban, no state targeting or police profiling of trans people, and no trans-specific violence data with a denominator. The real exposure is tier-3 societal hostility — documented discrimination in public spaces and government offices, frequent physical and sexual harassment of visibly trans people in provincial cities, rising anti-LGBT rhetoric from political leaders' supporters — with thin, undocumented recourse. Resident-facing LGR/care gaps are climate signals only. Sits modestly above the midpoint, materially below acceptance-with-working-protections jurisdictions.
